records.name: Guyana
records.summary_text:
Guyana is dangerous for trans visitors — one of only five Western-Hemisphere countries still criminalising same-sex conduct (buggery carries life imprisonment on paper, though rarely enforced). The IACHR heard evidence in November 2024 of severe violence against trans women: 69 cases of violence against trans women documented 2018–2022, in a country of under a million people. Police fail to investigate anti-LGBT violence; there is no anti-discrimination legislation (the UN Human Rights Committee called for it in April 2024) and no legal gender recognition.

records.name: Suriname
records.summary_text:
Suriname is a country that demands real caution from trans visitors — legally unremarkable, socially mixed. Same-sex conduct is legal, the constitution's 'any other status' clause is read to cover SOGI discrimination, and the penal code has carried sexual-orientation discrimination and hate-speech provisions since March 2015. There is no legal gender recognition and no documented trans-murder pattern, but the capital's small community reports routine harassment, and the interior has essentially no protection.
